historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2026 reported revenue growth (12.9% total, 16.7% commercial), decelerating
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs are not a usable growth anchor: the 5-year figure (32%) is dominated by the FY2023 capital raise (equity A$17.7m to A$65.4m), and the 3-year figure (11.5%) is retained profit off a small base that includes A$9.2m of deferred-tax-asset recognition. Revenue CAGRs (30% / 38%) reflect the FY2021-FY2024 US launch phase and overstate the forward rate: yearly growth has stepped down 58% (FY2024), 23% (FY2025), 13% (FY2026).
historical_growth.notes: EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: EPS was negative in FY2021 and FY2023, and owner FCF was negative in every year before FY2026 (FY2025: -A$10.8m reported). FY2026 is the first year of positive free cash flow and it is flattered by insurance cash and a working-capital release. Net SBC was a credit in FY2022, FY2025 and FY2026 because of forfeiture reversals, so the reported SBC series understates the ongoing grant cost; FY2021-FY2024 ran at 1.3-9% of revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: NovoSorb BTM keeps taking share in US burn and complex-wound surgery but at a maturing rate: FY2027 revenue growth of 12% reflects ~15% commercial growth offset by BARDA trial revenue running off (the contract ends September 2027) and the H2 FY2026 slowdown to ~8.5%. Growth holds in the low-to-mid teens through FY2030 as the US PMA for full-thickness burns, MTX and the outpatient/reimbursement push add indications, and rest-of-world markets (UK, India, Hong Kong, ANZ) compound off a small base, then fades to 4%. Revenue reaches ~A$364m by FY2036. The margin story is sales-force leverage: employee costs are 55% of revenue today, and EBITDA margin climbs from an underlying 9% to 25%, a normal level for a single-platform device company with a direct sales model. Capex steps down from the plant-build level; tax losses shelter the first few years only.
scenario_narratives.bull: The PMA for full-thickness burns is submitted by end CY2026 as guided and approved on a normal review clock, so the wider US label arrives in FY2028; that is why the 20% growth sits in years 2-3 and not year 1. Year 1 (17%) rests on what is already in hand: MTX (+93% constant currency in FY2026) and the FY2027 SynPath launch into the US outpatient channel. The CMS flat-rate payment framework for outpatient skin substitutes has been in force since 1 January 2026, so the reimbursement leg is no longer a policy outcome to wait for; what is unproven is coverage (the diabetic-foot and venous-leg-ulcer LCDs were withdrawn in December 2025) and whether a low-cost synthetic actually takes outpatient share at the flat rate. Revenue passes A$600m by FY2036. With the new Port Melbourne plant absorbing volume and the sales force already in place, incremental margins run near 40% and EBITDA margin reaches 30%. The case still needs a regulatory approval on time, outpatient uptake and two product launches, delivered by an executive team almost entirely new since 2025.
scenario_narratives.bear: BTM turns out to be largely penetrated in US burn centres, and the growth step-down seen in FY2024-FY2026 (58% to 23% to 13%) continues. US skin-substitute reimbursement tightening and competing dermal matrices cap pricing and outpatient adoption; the NHS and other public buyers stay budget-constrained; the PMA submission or its review slips. The leadership churn of 2025-2026 (CEO removed in March 2025, nine months under an acting CEO, a new CEO from December 2025, and a new Chair, General Counsel, CSO and Chief Quality Officer in the same window) shows up as execution cost: the SynPath outpatient launch underdelivers and the cost base keeps growing ahead of sales, as it did when the FY2026 EBITDA target was missed. Revenue grows 5-7% and reaches only ~A$225m by FY2036. The cost base, built for a much larger business, delivers little leverage, and EBITDA margin stalls at 15%. A second manufacturing site still has to be funded because of single-site concentration. The business survives, with net cash and positive cash flow, but is worth a fraction of today's price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: PolyNovo is valued as a growth-stage device company in a margin ramp, on a 10-year owner-FCF component build so that the terminal value capitalises a matured margin rather than today's 9%. Almost all of the value sits in the terminal year, so the valuation is a statement about two numbers: how large revenue gets and what EBITDA margin the direct-sales model settles at. House and street bases are close because SBC is about 1% of revenue.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal-heavy: the first five years contribute little free cash flow, so value depends on the mature EBITDA margin (25% base); each 5 points of terminal margin moves value by roughly a fifth
Growth deceleration: 58% to 23% to 13% over three years, with H2 FY2026 near 8.5%; the base case assumes this stabilises in the low teens

US concentration and reimbursement: ~75% of revenue is US. The CMS flat-rate outpatient skin-substitute payment has applied since 1 January 2026 and the related LCDs were withdrawn in December 2025; the base is inpatient-weighted and largely unaffected, but the SynPath outpatient push in the bull case depends on coverage that is not settled

Leadership and governance: CEO removed in March 2025 amid a board dispute, an acting CEO for nine months, a permanent CEO only since December 2025, and a new Chair, General Counsel, CSO and Chief Quality Officer. The margin ramp that carries the valuation is an execution task for a team with under a year together
PMA timing: the end-CY2026 milestone is a submission; approval follows FDA review, so label expansion cannot add revenue before FY2028 and a slip pushes the bull re-acceleration out year for year
Single manufacturing site at Port Melbourne; a second site would lift capex above the modelled path
FY2026 free cash flow (A$9.3m) is flattered by A$3.5m of insurance cash and a working-capital release and is not a run-rate
Carried-forward tax losses shelter early years only; the model ramps cash tax to 28% by year 5

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 0.81-1.298
data_sources.financials: PNV.AX_Metrics.csv and the FY2026 annual report (statements, notes 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 13, 21)
data_sources.qualitative: FY2026 annual report (CEO outlook, FY27 priorities, operating review, risk section); PNV.AX_Analysis.json (2026-11-15) reviewed after the build, text updated, drivers and weights unchanged

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 690.843m weighted ordinary shares + 7.354m dilutive options, FY2026 annual report note 10 (EPS). No shares issued in FY2026. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report note 6: gross share option expense recognised A$279k. The P&L line is a net CREDIT of A$458k because A$737k of previously recognised expense on forfeited options was reversed (FY2025: gross A$1,532k, net credit A$1,451k after A$3,061k of reversals on the former CEO's departure). The gross figure is used; a forfeiture reversal is not negative compensation. No equity-award withholding taxes in financing activities.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.4% + ~5.5% equity risk premium x beta ~1.1 (small-cap single-product medical device) = ~10.5% cost of equity. The company is debt-free in substance (A$3.6m equipment and insurance-premium finance against A$35.4m cash), so WACC = cost of equity = 10.5%. The same rate is used in all three scenarios; risk is carried in the flows and the weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B (leases as operating cost). Lease cash cost = principal A$1.565m + interest A$0.675m = A$2.24m in FY2026 (1.56% of revenue), charged through lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities of A$13.98m are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2026 total D&A A$3.456m less ROU depreciation ~A$1.3m = ~A$2.1m, 1.5% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: None. No non-controlling interest (the NCI in subsidiaries was acquired in earlier years; the equity reserve of A$9.294m is historical).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with the non-US adaptations (AUD WACC, lease treatment B, negative working-capital capture), 10-year horizon. Routed as a non-US operating company; it is not cyclical, so no mid-cycle normalisation applies. The feature that matters is that it is in a margin ramp: FY2026 underlying EBITDA was ~9% of revenue against a mature medical-device level in the mid-20s, so a 5-year horizon would capitalise an immature margin. FY0 MARGIN ANCHOR: reported EBITDA A$12.06m includes insurance claim income A$6.016m (R&D Innovation Centre fire), the related asset write-off A$4.717m, an unrealised FX loss A$2.678m and a net SBC credit A$0.458m. Stripping all four gives underlying pre-SBC EBITDA of ~A$13.0m, 9.0% of revenue (management's 'underlying EBITDA +50.4%' implies ~A$13.5m). FY0 FCF: reported A$9.312m = OCF A$23.109m - capex A$13.797m. OCF includes A$3.497m of one-off insurance cash and a working-capital release (inventories down A$4.7m, receivables down A$2.2m); capex is the tail of the new Port Melbourne plant. last_fcf follows the house identity (reported - SBC - interest income) and is NOT lease-adjusted; after the A$1.565m lease principal and the insurance receipt the repeatable figure is nearer A$4m. The projection does not start from last_fcf; it is rebuilt from components. REVENUE BASE: A$143.706m includes A$5.266m of BARDA cost-plus trial revenue (4% of sales, down 39%), which runs off by September 2027; commercial product sales were A$138.44m (+16.7% reported, +21.3% constant currency). H2 FY2026 total revenue grew ~8.5% on H2 FY2025 against ~18% in H1, part currency, part BARDA. TAX: A$50.5m of unrecognised and A$19m of recognised carried-forward losses (mostly Australian) shelter the early years; cash tax paid was A$1.0m in FY2026 (US). The cash tax path ramps 15% to 28% by year 5 and the shelter is not perpetuated. BUYBACKS: none, no dividend; the flat share count is a modelling convention, funded in the model by the SBC charge. No FY2027 revenue or EBITDA guidance is given in the annual report; the board's FY2026 STI EBITDA target was A$15.358m and was missed. QUALITATIVE REVIEW (2026-11-15): the drivers were built from the FY2026 annual report before PNV.AX_Analysis.json existed, then re-read against it. No driver path or weight was changed; the narratives, weights rationale and risk list were rewritten to state three things the annual report underplays: the breadth of the 2025-2026 leadership turnover, that the CMS outpatient skin-substitute payment framework is already in force (1 January 2026) rather than prospective, and that the PMA milestone guided for end CY2026 is a submission, so approval cannot help revenue before FY2028. What would move the numbers: FY2027 H1 commercial growth outside 10-18% (base year-1 and the bear/bull split), SynPath outpatient revenue disclosed at a material run-rate (bull years 1-3), an FDA refuse-to-file or major deficiency letter on the PMA (bear weight), or further C-suite departures under the new CEO (bear weight).

base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC, pre-lease-charge (post-IFRS-16) EBITDA. FY0 underlying 9.0%. Incremental underlying margin in FY2026 was ~27% (underlying EBITDA up ~A$4.5m on revenue up A$16.5m); the path assumes incremental margins of 30-40% as the direct sales force (employee cost is 55% of revenue) is leveraged.
base.wc_note: Negative: receivables A$22.2m + inventories A$9.8m - payables A$16.8m = A$15.2m, 10.6% of revenue. Growth consumes cash.
base.capex_note: FY2025 and FY2026 ran at ~A$13.9m (9.6-11% of revenue) building the new Port Melbourne plant, now complete pending regulatory approval. 'Augment manufacturing footprint' is an FY2027 priority (single-site concentration is a stated risk), so capex is held above maintenance for three years.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: growth has decelerated three years running, H2 FY2026 grew only ~8.5%, the FY2026 EBITDA target was missed, ~75% of revenue comes from one product in one country exposed to US reimbursement policy, and leadership has turned over almost completely in 18 months (CEO removed March 2025, acting CEO for nine months, permanent CEO only since December 2025; Chair, General Counsel, CSO and Chief Quality Officer all new). Base held at 50%. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs a PMA approval, outpatient uptake and successful second-product launches together. Reviewed against the qualitative analysis on 2026-11-15 and left at 25/50/25: the two new facts pull in opposite directions and neither is large. The CMS outpatient framework being live since January 2026 removes one policy contingency from the bull (the rule exists and a flat per-cm2 rate favours a low-cost synthetic), but coverage is unsettled after the LCD withdrawal and PolyNovo has no outpatient revenue to show yet. The PMA is a submission in CY2026, not an approval, so its benefit is a FY2028+ event already placed in bull years 2-3. Leadership turnover is wider than 'the CEO has changed' implied, but it was the reason for part of the original bear uplift, the new team has been in place for most of a year, and a further uplift would double-count the missed EBITDA target and growth slowdown that are its visible effects. The share-price fall and sell-side target cuts are not evidence about cash flows and carry no weight here.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
